_README: Objections and questions raised against specific sentences, which travel WITH
the sentence into the review document instead of living in an email thread.
A note appears on its row, in red, above the text it concerns. The reviewer
reads the objection and the sentence together and types the correction in the
same place. Nothing is guessed at on their behalf.
`id` is the eight-character code shown on the row in the document, and it is
stable across re-exports because it is derived from the string's position in
the source rather than from its content. Find one with:
Delete a note once it has been resolved. This file is committed, so the
history of what was challenged and by whom is kept.

notes.note: THE NAME IS WRONG. Kevin Bennet: "we are reinventing history by stating that the Precision Surgery Laboratories (of only Kendall Lee) developed the equipment. This is not true. It was created by the Neural Engineering Laboratory of which I was co-Founder and Co-Director for about 18 years." Please write the correct name of the laboratory here. Note it is used in four other places, listed below.
THE NAME IS WRONG — see the note on the heading above. The founding, the co-directorship and the 18 years are yours to state correctly; please rewrite this entry.

WHO BUILT THE PROTOTYPE. Kevin Bennet: "The Division of Engineering designed and built the original working prototypes and the MAVEN software - of which I chaired for 20 years, which NaviNetics licensed from Mayo." This entry currently credits the laboratory. Please rewrite it so the Division of Engineering is credited, and say whether the licence from Mayo should be stated here or on its own.
THE NAME IS WRONG — same correction as the company timeline. This sentence also says the NRSS was prototyped in the laboratory; if the Division of Engineering built it, this needs to change too.
